note: Window agent p1730-p1739, 2 Nov 2026. keyframe_overrides/3 and /4 (Akwamu, Akyem Abuakwa) replace two dossier keyframes whose region named the town 'Akwamufie', unknown to the gazetteer, so the keyframes and the 1730 loss and gain events were skipped and Akwamu stayed at its 1702 peak shape (77 cells) to 1886. The two overrides run to 1886 and 1851, the dossiers' own spans, so they reach beyond the window. events/2 (Kartli vassalage) has no vassal_end: the page dates it 1736 to 1747, so a vassal_end in 1747 belongs to p1740-p1749. Reviewer (2 Nov 2026): events/3 added, the vassal_end of 1747 that closes events/2 (dated outside the window, in p1740-p1749's years); first sentences of the notes of events/0, /1 and /2 rewritten as historical statements, since the compiler takes a caption from each note's first sentence.

region.text: the Habsburg lands outside the Austro-Turkish theatre that the war's region spec swept in: Silesia and Bohemian-Moravian Silesia (Poland, Czechia), border cells of Germany, Upper Austria

events.note: 1737: the stakes of the Austro-Turkish War (1737-1739) are the Kingdom of Serbia with Belgrade, the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia) and the Bosnian section of Posavina, the three regions the Habsburgs ceded at Belgrade on 18 September 1739. The habsburg-monarchy contest_start of 1737 is drawn on 'the Habsburg shape of 1738 minus its 1741 shape', which also takes in Silesia and Upper Austria (lost in 1741-42), so 219 cells of Poland, Czechia, Germany and Austria are striped as contested with the Ottomans in 1737-1739. The Treaty of Belgrade page names only Serbia and Belgrade, the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia) and the Bosnian Posavina as the contested and ceded ground; fighting is described at Grocka and Belgrade (21-22 July 1739) and nothing in Silesia, Bohemia or Moravia. A contest_end closes the whole pair, so events/1 re-opens it on the theatre cells; the Serbian, Banat and Oltenian cells stay contested to 18 September 1739. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: first sentence added so the map caption is a historical statement; the rest unchanged.]

region.text: northern Serbia, Belgrade, the Banat and Oltenia and the Bosnian Posavina: the dossier's own region without Silesia and Upper Austria

events.note: 1737: the war zone is northern Serbia with Belgrade and Oltenia; the Habsburg army is beaten at Grocka on 21-22 July 1739 and then besieged in the Belgrade Fortress. Re-opens the Austro-Turkish contest of 1737-1739 on the theatre alone, after events/0 closed it: a contest_end closes the whole pair, not just the cells of its region. The Treaty of Belgrade page: the Habsburgs ceded the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia), the Kingdom of Serbia with Belgrade and the Bosnian section of Posavina; the fighting it describes is at Grocka and Belgrade in July 1739. The dossier's contest_end of 18 September 1739 (habsburg-monarchy/ledger/77) closes it again. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: first sentence added so the map caption is a historical statement; the rest unchanged.]

region.text: Kartli (the kingdom-of-kartli shape of 1706, carried to 1762)

events.note: 1736: the Ottomans give up Kartli, which is again a vassal state of Persia from 1736 to 1747. The Kingdom of Kartli page's infobox reads 'Vassal state of Persia: 1555-1578; 1612-1723; 1736-1747', and 'In 1736 Turkey ... gave up Kartli and Kakhetia'. The draft ends the Ottoman occupation in 1736 (kingdom-of-kartli/ledger/8) but then draws Kartli as an independent state, so it wins every conflict against the Afsharid claim as a free kingdom. This opens the Persian vassalage of 1736; the page closes it in 1747 (events/3, added by the reviewer, closes it in 1747). [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: first sentence added for the caption; without a vassal_end the relation stayed open to 1762, since the dossier's 1747 vassal_end (afsharid-iran/ledger/25) names kingdom-of-georgia, not kingdom-of-kartli.]

events.note: 1747: after Nader Shah's assassination Teimuraz II and his son Heraclius II, given the kingships of Kartli and Kakheti by Nader, declare their de facto independence from Persia. Closes the Persian vassalage that events/2 opens in 1736: the Kingdom of Kartli page's infobox reads 'Vassal state of Persia: ... 1736-1747', and 'In 1747, the Shah of Persia, Nader Shah was assassinated'; 'Capitalizing on this instability Teimuraz II and his son Heraclius II ... declared their de facto independence from Persia.' The dossier's own vassal_end of 1747 (afsharid-iran/ledger/25) names kingdom-of-georgia (ended 1478), so it closes nothing and Kartli stayed an Afsharid vassal to 1762 in a trial of p1740-p1749. Added by the reviewer of p1730-p1739; dated in p1740-p1749's years. No month on the page: it takes the month of the dossier's last 1747 event.

region.text: Afghanistan except the northern provinces Baghlan, Balkh, Samangan and Sari Pul (the Kabul, Ghazni, Jalalabad, Bamyan and Kandahar country that Nader's army took in 1738)

rulings.why: In 1738 the size rule gives 417 cells claimed by both the Afsharid keyframe and the Mughal one to the smaller Mughal state; the Mughal keyframe of 1738 then drops them, so about 400 cells of Afghanistan (Kandahar, Bamyan, Wardak, Nangarhar, Laghman, Parwan and others) end 1738 and 1739 as nobody's land. The page has Nader take Kandahar, reach Ghazni on 11 June and Kabul (citadel capitulated 19 June 1738), sack Jalalabad on 7 September, occupy Peshawar after 6 November, and send a detachment against 'the Afghans of Ghorband and Bamian'. The northern provinces are left out: the page gives no 1738 action there.
